content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a new semi-supervised action detection algorithm. Semi-supervised learning on action detection is hard because the generated pseudo label is normally low-quality. Built upon the classic Mean Teacher, authors propose to train an auxiliary network that learns to refine the detection results of student network on labeled data, which is then used to refine the pseudo label produced by the teacher network on unlabeled data. Experimental results show an advantage of adding the auxiliary module. Besides, the authors also discuss which kind of consistency (classification and localization) to train on, as well as different kinds of data augmentation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
+ The proposed method is sensible. 

+ The related work is introduced properly.

- The auxiliary module is designed to learn to refine the detection results on labeled data, which in turn can refine the output from teacher network and give better pseudo labels on unlabeled data. However, this can also be accomplished by removing the auxiliary module while adding the same amount of parameters into the base model, i.e., training a bigger model with regular mean teacher. Since bigger model can also give better output, the teacher will give better pseudo labels in this case as well. A comparison to this baseline (removing the auxiliary module, but using larger base model to keep the same number of parameters) would be helpful.

- The authors may also need to consider the impact of backbone architecture. In this work VideoCapsuleNet is used for base model and a 3d U-Net is used for the auxiliary model. Is it possible that the improvement is brought by the advantage of the U-Net architecture? What if we use a U-Net as base model as well?

- Is there any insight on why adding the constraint of classification consistency will harm the performance? Is it because the labels are biased?

- In Section 4.2, "Base vs Enhanced Mean Teacher", the authors claim that "There’s a performance boost of 10-12% on
UCF101-24 and 6-8% on JHMDB-21 at the 0.5 thresholds". Could you explain how this is calculated? For example, Table 1 shows that the base mean teacher achieves 65.4 f-mAP@0.5 on UCF101-24, and Table 3 shows the enhanced version reaches 66.8 on the same metric. That's improvement of 1.4. Where does the 10-12% improvement come from?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The presentation is clear and easy to follow. The method seems simple enough to reproduce. Comparison to some baselines is missing.
content.summary_of_the_review: The motivation is clear and the proposed method is sensible. However, comparison to some baselines is needed to show that the idea of adding an auxiliary module to refine the pseudo label could be helpful for the task.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

replying_to: Replying to Learning from student's mistakes: Improving mean teacher for end-to-end semi-supervised video action detection
display_title: Official Review of Paper3730 by Reviewer wMms

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
In this paper, the authors tackle the problem of semi-supervised video action detection. They propose to employ a student-teacher based semi-supervised learning for the task. They introduce an auxiliary module, 3D UNet, to provide further consistency supervision to the model. The auxiliary module enhances the action localization maps of student and teacher. They also employ temporal and spatial augmentations to achieve robustness. The proposed method is validated on two small-scale public benchmarks: UCF-101-24 and JHMDB-21. The claimed contributions are as follows:

C1. They propose a student-teacher based approach for semi-supervised video action recognition task.

C2. They propose an auxiliary module that learns from student’s mistakes to improve the teacher.

C3. They conduct an extensive empirical analysis of consistency losses.

C4. They show some insights about the proposed method by using spatial and temporal augmentations.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
This paper has the following strengths.

S1. The problem they tackle, semi-supervised video action detection is important as spatio-temporal action annotation is extremely expensive. 

S2. The proposed method shows favorable performance compared with state-of-the-art methods.

However, this paper has several weaknesses as well.
W1. Unfair comparison with state-of-the-art. 
They employ strong augmentations, which is not their contribution: temporal drop out, temporal reversal, Gaussian blur, horizontal flip, grayscale, hue/saturation/brightness/contrast adjustments and these augmentations would give some performance boost as shown in the literature [1,2]. That means the strong augmentations could benefit compared methods as well. In my opinion, there should be an ablation experiment showing the performance of the proposed method without strong augmentation or with less strong augmentations. On the other way around, when comparing with state-of-the-art such as [Kumar & Rawat 2022], the strong augmentations should be employed in both methods. 

[1] FixMatch: Simplifying Semi-Supervised Learning with Consistency and Confidence, Sohn et al., NeurIPS 2020.
[2] Learning Representational Invariances for Data-Efficient Action Recognition, Zou, et al., arXiv preprint arXiv:2103.16565 (2021).

W2. The core contribution seems weak.
The authors claim that the teacher learns from student’s mistakes. I think this is an overclaim. As shown in Figure 2, there is no gradient flow from the auxiliary module to the teacher. Teacher might implicitly learn by EMA of student. However, this learning also applies to other EMA-based student-teacher learning methods.

Empirically, in Table 3, the authors ablate their core contribution, the auxiliary module. L_2 + Aux-S shows 0.2 points f-mAP@0.5, 0.1 points v-mAP@0.2 improvement on the UCF101-24 and shows 1.1 points f-mAP@0.5, 0.7 point v-mAP@0.5 drop on the JHMDB-21 compared to the L2 baseline. I do not see clear gain from the proposed auxiliary module.

W3. Presentation quality
There are many errors such as inconsistent numbers, wrong/awkward sentences, and typos throughout the paper. To list a few below:

1) In Table 2, “Ours” shows 67.4% f-mAP@0.5 and 95.0%/67.2% v-mAP@0.2/0.5 on the JHMDB-51 while it shows 64.7% f-mAP@0.5 and 96.9%/64.4% v-mAP@0.2/0.5 in Table 3. 

2) Aux-L does not show the best score among the three variations in Table 3 which contradicts the second paragraph of Section 4.2.


There are some clarification questions for the authors.

Q1. “This ensures that the improvement of pseudo-labels is not dependent on the input video and is sample agnostic” -> I do not understand this. Why this is the case?

Q2. What are the ablation results of all four losses other than supervised classification and localization losses employed? 

Q3. What is the random probability map in the spatial augmentations?

Q4. I do not understand the last sentence in Section 4.2. Why do we need to interpolate frames?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper combines many existing ideas: mean-teacher, strong augmentation, and 3D UNet. It is okay to combine many ideas if the motivation is reasonable and it brings some new insight. However, this paper lacks any reasonable motivation or new insight. Therefore, I would say the paper is not very novel. The performance improvement from the core contribution seems quite weak as I stated in the weaknesses part. Therefore, the quality is low as well. There are many errors and inconsistencies in the paper. Therefore it is not clear.
content.summary_of_the_review: Despite its favorable performance compared to the state-of-the-art methods, this paper lacks novelty, quality and the clarity. Therefore I would recommend this paper a reject.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors present a method to perform semi-supervised video action detection using a student-teacher framework. The student network trains on a combination of ground-truth labels of the labeled data and pseudo-labels provided by the teacher for the unlabeled data. An auxiliary learning module takes in the student's mistakes to make the teacher predict more accurate pseudo-labels for the student, thereby progressing the end-to-end training. The authors demonstrate the benefits of the individual components of their method through multiple experiments and provide some analysis of their performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strengths**
1. The proposed student-teacher framework for semi-supervised learning makes good sense, especially with the auxiliary learning module that gradually improves the teacher's predictions based on the student's mistakes.

2. The experimental results are comprehensive and ablation studies and analysis subsections provide additional insight into how the individual components of the method work.

3. The paper is clearly written overall and easy to follow.

4. The discussion of the limitations helps to understand the scope of the work.


**Weaknesses**

The authors specifically talk about temporal and spatial augmentations as part of their contributions, but the nature of these contributions is not clear to me.

1. Is the sequence of augmentations (Sec. 3.3) relevant other than to reduce the operational costs of spatial augmentation?

2. How is temporal reversal a relevant augmentation? Reversal can potentially change the action itself (e.g., jumping up becomes falling down), does it make sense to train with such "incorrect" actions?

3. What are the marginal benefits of using consistent and random skip rates for temporal augmentation? Is it possible to just use one of them without any significant drop in performance?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
**Clarity**

Why do the authors use the same decay rate $\beta$ for the teacher (Eqn. 1) and the auxiliary (Eqn. 2) modules?

**Quality and Novelty**

The comprehensive results support the quality of the contributions. The auxiliary module acting as "feedback" from the student to improve the teacher is novel and makes intuitive sense.


**Reproducibility**

The authors have clearly explained all the components of their method and provided implementation details, making their work reproducible.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, the proposed method is novel, sound, and well-supported by the experimental results. Their method sets a new benchmark for video action detection and can be reused for associated applications.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a mean teacher approach for semi-supervised video action detection. The idea is to train identical teacher and student networks with weakly and strongly augmented data, respectively. Teachers' weights are updated via Exponential Moving Average. The student network is also trained by the spatiotemporal pseudo-labeled data by the teacher network. In addition, the predictions of both networks are fed into auxiliary networks that are trained using classification and localization-level consistency. Extensive experiments on three different datasets, UCF101-24, JHMDB-21, and YouTube-VOS, show the efficiency of the proposed approach over recent semi-supervised approaches.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strength:**
1. Supervised DL-based video action detection approaches require many labeled samples. Weakly and semi- supervised methods are promising to reduce the need for labeled data. Mean teacher approach has been applied to different problems but is limited in the video domain, and this paper addresses this gap.

2. Experimental results are convincing, and the proposed method outperforms previous state-of-the-, semi-supervised methods in UCF101-24, JHMDB-21, and YouTube-VOS datasets.

**Weaknesses:**
1. Kumar and Rawat (2022) have been used to have a comparable baseline, VideoCapsuleNet; however, the similarities between the two works have not been properly stated. As far as I understood, it has the same workflow; however, one branch takes original samples, and the other takes augmented versions. Supervised terms and classification and spatiotemporal consistency losses are taken from this study. The major differences in this study are to have the data weakly and strongly supervised in respective branches and mean teacher loss to learn from the strongly augmented student branch via exponential moving average. 

2. Learning between two different augmented versions of the data, relational SSL had already applied a very similar approach; however, not cited. This work applies what is proposed in the paper; the only difference is its being in the image domain:
Zheng, et al., ReSSL: Relational Self-Supervised Learning with Weak Augmentation, NeurIPS 2021, https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2021/hash/14c4f36143b4b09cbc320d7c95a50ee7-Abstract.html

3. The major difference in comparison with Tarvainen and Valpola (2017) is the weak and strong augmentations in the two branches. I found this as a limited contribution as the proposed study shows strong similarities with Kumar and Rawat (2022), and the only difference is the mean teacher approach.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is written clearly, and the approach is described in a detailed way that makes the experiments reproducible. However, the algorithmic novelty is quite limited, and the similarities (particularly consistency losses) with Kumar and Rawat (2022) are not covered in the text in a transparent way.
content.summary_of_the_review: I think the overall contribution and algorithmic novelty are limited. Due to the points sated above, I consider this work marginally below the acceptance threshold.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
